To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the 20‐kDa homologous restriction protein (HRF20, CD59) is localized in the pericapillary region and the mesangial matrix of normal glomeruli.
the HRF20 (20‐kD membrane protein) is present in normal human glomeruli, and that its expression is enhanced in the cases of lupus nephritis with subendothelial deposits.
HRF20 is expressed in the glomeruli of normal kidneys as well as in diseased kidneys, but its expression is enhanced in the glomerular endothelial cells of the kidneys with subendothelial deposits.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of complement and the regulation of complement activation in the glomeruli.
the localization of 20‐kd homologous restriction factors in human glomerular disease.
the localization of HFR20 in human glomeluronephritis, especially lupus nephritis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
HRF20 is a normal component of human glomerular capillaries.
HRF20 is not a component of MAC but is present in human glomeruli.
HRF20 is a ubiquitous protein and its expression in glomeruli is enhanced in certain diseases.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HRF20 is not only present in the glomerular basement membrane but also in the mesangium, and the amount of HRF20 may be increased in the glomeruli of the cases with lupus nephritis.
HRF20 is expressed in glomerular cells and its expression is increased in lupus nephritis.
the expression of HRF20 (20‐kD protein) is increased under conditions where complement is activated.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HRF20 may play an important role in the pathophysiology of glomerular diseases and the deposition of MAC in glomerular diseases.
HRF20 is a useful marker for the study of human glomerulopathies.
HRF20 is present in the normal kidney but its expression is increased in the glomerular diseases with immune deposits.
